faq: Do I need to be sending already?
No. If you are starting from nothing, we plan a gentle rhythm that fits your list size. If you already send, we use your past results to place the best days and topics.
How many emails should I send each week?

It depends on your list, products and how people respond. We usually suggest a rhythm you can keep up, such as one to two emails a week, and show how to adjust it using your open and unsubscribe numbers.
Does the calendar include the written emails?
It includes a brief for each send: the subject idea, main message and offer. The finished copy and design are separate services, and you can order them with this one.
Will it work for seasonal businesses?
Yes. We build around your busy and quiet periods, and plan warm-up sends before peak weeks. Tell us when your year gets busy in the order form.

desc:
An email and SMS campaign calendar tells you what to send, to whom and when, so no send is planned the night before. Ecom Swift LLC builds a shareable calendar with topics, audiences, offers and short briefs that your team can follow week after week.

## Why does a campaign calendar matter?

A campaign calendar matters because it replaces last-minute guessing with a plan. It lists every planned send with its date, channel, audience, offer and goal. Your team can see the whole month at a glance, spot gaps and avoid sending the same message twice.

Without a plan, stores tend to send in bursts: five messages for a sale, then silence for weeks. Subscribers forget you during the silence and tire of you during the burst. A calendar spreads sends sensibly and keeps your brand in view without crowding the inbox.

## How planning improves your results

Good timing and good targeting come from preparation. When the sale date, product launch and restock are known weeks ahead, the copy, images and links can be ready, tested and approved without panic. Mistakes such as wrong links or expired offers usually come from rushing.

Planning also protects subscribers. A calendar sets sending limits, so one person does not receive an email, a text and a second email in a single afternoon. Fewer unsubscribes and fewer spam complaints help your sender reputation, which in turn helps future messages reach the inbox. Outcomes still depend on your list, offers and products, but a plan removes avoidable waste.

## What a useful campaign calendar contains

- Key dates for your business: launches, sales, restocks, holidays and slow weeks.
- A send date and time for each message, with the time zone noted.
- The channel for each send: email, SMS or both.
- The audience: all subscribers, recent buyers, a collection fan group or a specific segment.
- The offer or message angle, written in one clear line.
- A goal for each send, such as clicks to a collection or sales of one product.
- A short brief explaining what the message should say and which link to use.
- Rest days and quiet weeks, so subscribers are not overloaded.
- A column for status: idea, drafted, approved, scheduled, sent.
- Notes on what to measure afterwards, so the next plan learns from the last.

## How we plan it with you

We start with a short conversation about your products, seasons, past sales and any dates you already know. If you have sent campaigns before, we look at which sends earned attention and which were ignored. If you have not sent anything yet, we plan from your catalog and your goals.

The calendar is built in a sheet that you can share with your team. The Basic package gives one month with a topic for each send. Standard adds audiences, offers and a short brief for each campaign across email and SMS. Premium plans three months, including launch and sale sequences, sending limits and a review call. We do not write the full emails in this service, but each brief says enough that a writer or designer can start straight away.

## Planning habits to follow and avoid

**Do:**
- Plan around real dates, such as launches and stock arrivals.
- Match each send to one audience and one goal.
- Leave space between promotions so full-price products get attention too.
- Mark a deadline for copy and images before each send date.
- Compare each result with the plan and adjust the next month.

**Avoid:**
- Filling every day just because the calendar has space.
- Sending the same offer to everyone, every time.
- Texting for low-value news that email could carry.
- Changing the plan without telling the team.
- Treating the calendar as fixed when sales data says otherwise.

## Who this is for

A small store owner who sends when inspiration strikes can use this to build a steady rhythm. A seller with a busy season ahead can plan the launch and sale sequence well before it starts. A team of two or three people sharing the work can use one sheet as the single source of truth, so nobody wonders who is sending what.

## What we need from you

Share your store link, a list of your best-selling products or collections, important dates and any promotions already planned. If you send already, tell us which tool you use and roughly how often. We never need passwords. If we need to look at past results, access is given as a collaborator, staff or team user, and you stay the owner of your account.
